apollo_11.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module (Eagle) & EASEP
apollo_11.current_status: Descent stage and EASEP remain at Tranquility Base (EASEP terminated Aug 27, 1969). Ascent stage jettisoned July 22, 1969 and assumed impacted on the Moon.

apollo_12.name: Apollo 12 Lunar Module (Intrepid) & ALSEP

surface_stats.notable_event: Visited Surveyor 3 and returned ~10 kg of parts (camera and soil scoop) to Earth.

apollo_12.current_status: Descent stage remains at landing site. Ascent stage intentionally crashed into Moon on Nov 20, 1969 (3.94 S, 338.80 E). ALSEP shut down Sept 30, 1977.

apollo_15.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Module (Falcon), LRV & ALSEP
apollo_15.mission_type: Crewed Lunar Module, Rover & Surface Experiments

surface_stats.eva_duration: 18 hours 35 minutes (3 EVAs + 33 min standup EVA)
surface_stats.notable_event: First deployment of the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV); hammer-and-feather vacuum drop test.

apollo_15.current_status: Descent stage and LRV parked permanently on the Moon. Ascent stage impacted Moon on Aug 3, 1971 (26.36 N, 0.25 E). ALSEP shut down Sept 30, 1977.

surveyor_3.name: Surveyor 3 (Surveyor-C)
instruments: Surface Sampler (5 ft reach, dug 4 trenches up to 7 inches deep)
surveyor_3.highlights: Bounced twice during landing (10 m and 3 m) due to radar confusion. Measured lunar soil bearing strength at ~10 psi (98 kPa), proving it could support an Apollo Lunar Module. Visited by Apollo 12 astronauts in Nov 1969.
surveyor_3.current_status: Inactive on the Moon; last contact May 4, 1967.

mars_pathfinder_sojourner.name: Mars Pathfinder (Carl Sagan Memorial Station) & Sojourner Rover
mars_pathfinder_sojourner.launch_site: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida
mars_pathfinder_sojourner.highlights: Delivered Sojourner, the first-ever rover on Mars, using an innovative 17-foot multi-lobed airbag system that bounced ~15 times. Returned 2.3 billion bits of data, 16,500 lander images, 550 rover images, and 15 chemical rock analyses confirming a warmer, wetter Martian past.
mars_pathfinder_sojourner.current_status: Permanently parked in Ares Vallis; final transmission Sept 27, 1997.

spirit_and_opportunity.name: Mars Exploration Rovers (MER): Spirit & Opportunity
spirit_and_opportunity.highlights: Designed for 90-sol missions, both rovers operated for years and found clear geological evidence of past liquid water on Mars. Opportunity drove over 45 km across Meridiani Planum.
spirit_and_opportunity.current_status: Inactive monuments on Mars. Spirit last communicated March 22, 2010; Opportunity lost contact during a global dust storm in June 2018 (mission ended Feb 2019).

viking_1.name: Viking 1 Lander & Orbiter
viking_1.highlights: First U.S. spacecraft to land safely and operate on Mars. Conducted biological soil experiments searching for life and captured the first high-resolution color panoramas of the Martian surface. Operated on the surface for 2,245 sols.
viking_1.current_status: Lander remains stationary at Chryse Planitia (last contact Nov 1982). Orbiter terminated Aug 17, 1980.

insight.name: InSight Mars Lander (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport)
instruments: Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package (HP3)
insight.highlights: First mission dedicated to studying Mars' deep interior (crust, mantle, and core). Detected over 1,300 marsquakes (up to magnitude 5) and tracked meteoroid impacts.
insight.current_status: Inactive on Elysium Planitia; lost power due to dust buildup on its solar panels (mission ended Dec 21, 2022).

dawn.name: Dawn Spacecraft
dawn.highlights: First spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies, first to orbit a main-belt asteroid (Vesta), and first to visit a dwarf planet (Ceres).
dawn.current_status: Depleted its hydrazine fuel on Oct 31, 2018; remains in a perpetual, unpowered orbit around Ceres.

ingenuity.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
ingenuity.highlights: First aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet. Planned for 5 flights over 30 days, it completed 72 flights across nearly three years as an aerial scout for Perseverance.
ingenuity.current_status: Sustained rotor damage during its 72nd landing on Jan 18, 2024 (mission ended Jan 25, 2024). Stationary artifact in Neretva Vallis.

kepler.name: Kepler Space Telescope (Kepler / K2)
kepler.highlights: NASA's first planet-hunting telescope; discovered thousands of exoplanets and proved that planets outnumber stars in the Milky Way. Operated an extended K2 mission after reaction wheel failures.
kepler.current_status: Ran out of fuel and retired on Oct 30, 2018; drifting safely in an Earth-trailing orbit around the Sun.

near_shoemaker.name: NEAR Shoemaker (Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous)
near_shoemaker.highlights: First spacecraft to orbit and successfully touch down on an asteroid (433 Eros), despite not being originally built as a lander.
near_shoemaker.current_status: Permanently resting on the surface of asteroid 433 Eros (last contact Feb 28, 2001).

pioneer_10_11.name: Pioneer 10 & Pioneer 11
pioneer_10_11.highlights: First spacecraft to traverse the asteroid belt and make close flybys of Jupiter (Pioneer 10 & 11) and Saturn (Pioneer 11). Both carry gold-anodized Pioneer Plaques depicting humanity.
pioneer_10_11.current_status: Unpowered and drifting silently out of the solar system into interstellar space.
